_comment: Copy this file to config/tokens.json and fill in real values.
config/tokens.json is git-ignored and docker-ignored: it is mounted at runtime, never baked into the image.
Each token authorizes writes (upload, delete) to exactly one bucket. Callers send it as: Authorization: Bearer <bucket>:<token>
The general TOKEN env var keeps working everywhere and is the only credential accepted on the /aws, /minio, /monitor and /metrics routes.
Tokens must be at least 32 characters, so copying this file unedited fails at boot on purpose. Generate one with: openssl rand -hex 32
Bucket names must be 3-63 characters of lowercase letters, digits or '-'.
expires_at is optional (RFC 3339). Omit it for a token that never expires. It is checked per request, so an expired token stops working without a restart.
The file is read once at boot; restart the service after editing it.

buckets.label: optional note about who uses this token
